notes: Source: 2026 Seattle Seahawks Media Guide (IA item seattle-seahawks-2026-media-guide, dated 2026-09-09). The regular-season individual records are pdf p331-340 ('INDIVIDUAL RECORDS - REGULAR SEASON'): rushing pdf p332-333, passing pdf p333-334, receiving pdf p334-335, interceptions pdf p335, sacks and tackles pdf p339. The guide prints no page numbers, so pdf_page is the PDF page. Postseason records (pdf p349-352), opponent records (the 'OPPONENT INDIVIDUAL RECORDS' blocks on the same pages) and team records (pdf p341-348) were not used.

through_season 2025: the lists contain 2025 entries (Jaxon Smith-Njigba 119 receptions and 1,793 yards in 2025, Jason Myers' 2025 kicking records, 'Last: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, 2025') and the guide's own team-record pages cite 11/30/2025 and 1/3/2026 games.

The guide prints NO rank numbers. Each list is three value tiers: the value (or record) is printed once on the first line of a tier and further names sharing it follow on lines with a blank value cell. Rank here = competition ranking over the printed rows (tied rows share the lower rank and carry tie=true); in `raw`, a value in [square brackets] is the tier value printed on the line above (blank cell on this row). Lists run past three rows where a tier has several names.

A printed line that gives two or more seasons for one player ('Shaun Alexander, 2002, 2004'; 'Russell Wilson, 2015, 2017'; 'Richard Sherman, 2012, 2013') became one row per season with the whole printed line in raw; those rows are tied with each other.

Aggregate tiers ('3 - 16 Times (Last: Kenneth Walker III, at Detroit 9/30/24)' for game rushing TDs; '3 - 11 Times (Last: DK Metcalf, at Dallas 11/30/2023)' for game receiving TDs) name no single record holder and are not rows. The game touchdown-pass list is the exception: the guide prints only '5 - 11 Times (Last: Russell Wilson, vs. Dallas, 9/27/2020)', so that list has one row (the named last game, tie=true) and its scope_note says so; the other ten five-TD games are not named in the guide.

Game lists: `years` is the printed date (M/D/YYYY) followed by the printed opponent text ('11/11/2001 vs. Oakland'); raw keeps the line as printed. '(OT)' is kept as printed. Career `years` are the printed spans ('2012-21, 2023' for Bobby Wagner). Lists headed only 'Most Touchdowns, Career/Season/Game' sit under the RUSHING or RECEIVING heading (titles carry the section in brackets); the scoring section on pdf p331 has separate total-touchdown lists that were not used.

Sacks: the career list marks Jacob Green 97.5 with '*' and the footnote '*Unofficially 116.0. Sacks did not become official until 1982.', so the 97.5 is the official count (value used); every season/game sack entry is 1983 or later. Tackles: the guide labels none of its tackle lists solo/total/unofficial; they are team-counted totals.

Verification: every digit was read from 200 dpi crops of the page pictures, then each list was compared by script with the Internet Archive OCR text of the same page (work/agent_SEA/verify_sea.py and verify_block.py): every number, date and surname of all 108 rows occurs there, and 29 of the 30 lists occur as one contiguous block in the same order (the 30th, season interceptions, differs only because the OCR text reads 'Darryl!' for 'Darryl'). The tiers also agree with other printed lists: the scoring-section totals on pdf p331 split into rushing + receiving touchdowns exactly as listed here (Alexander 112 = 100 + 12, Largent 101 = 1 + 100, Lynch 66 = 58 + 8, Alexander 2005 28 = 27 + 1) and Largent's 819 receptions / 13,089 yards match the average-per-reception line on pdf p335.
